questions.stem: I-125 labelled albumin is used for measurement of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Plasma volume

I-125 labelled albumin is the most commonly used substance for measurement of plasma volume.

questions.stem: Which hormone is required to cross the plasma membrane for its actions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thyroxine
  • The hormone that is required to cross the plasma membrane for its actions is B. Thyroxine.
  • For its actions, thyroxine needs to cross the plasma membrane and bind to nuclear receptors, which then modulate gene expression and cellular activities.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 296 and 362, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no: 998, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no. 930 and 933.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an example of a feed forward mechanism?

options.label: D
options.text: Exercise resulting in heart rate increase

questions.answerText: Exercise resulting in heart rate increase
questions.solutionHtml:
Exercise resulting in heart rate increase

Exercise resulting in heart rate increase is not an example of feedforward control mechanism. However, thinking about exercise and it resulting in a heart rate increase would be an example of feedforward control mechanism.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no. 9, 10, Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page nos 129, 245

Pre-Botzinger complex

The Pre-Botzinger complex is a group of neurons located in the medulla oblongata, specifically in the ventrolateral region. It plays a crucial role in the generation of the rhythmic breathing pattern, including the initiation of inspiration.



Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page nos 646.

questions.stem: Measurement of anatomical dead space is done by?
questions.solutionHtml:
Single breath N2 washout method

The single breath nitrogen (N2) washout method is a technique used to measure the anatomical dead space in the respiratory system. It is based on the principle that the first portion of the exhaled breath, which primarily consists of air from the anatomical dead space, contains a higher concentration of nitrogen compared to the alveolar air.



Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page nos 622.

questions.stem: Which is not a monomeric intermediate filament?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tubulin

Filamentous proteins are of three types:

  • Microfilaments are polymers of the protein actin and are 7 nm in diameter.
  • Microtubules are composed of tubulin and are 25 nm in diameter.
  • Intermediate filaments are composed of various proteins, depending on the type of cell in which they are found; they are normally 8-12 nm in diameter

Intermediate filaments ae the most abundant cytoskeletal filament. They are primarily the structural proteins of all maintaining cellular architecture.

Intermediate filaments include:

  • Desmin
  • Keratin
  • Neurofibrillary Acidic Protein
  • Vimentin
  • Laminin
  • Neurofilaments

Tubulin is the protein that polymerizes into long chains or filaments that form microtubules

There are five different types of Intermediate filaments:

  • Types I and II: Acidic Keratin and Basic Keratin, respectively
  • Type III
  • Type IV Neurofilament H (heavy), M (medium) and L (low)
  • Type V are the lamins which have a nuclear signal sequence so they can form a filamentous support inside the inner nuclear membrane.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no. 71, Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th - 'ition Page no. 105

questions.stem: Hepcidin acts on which receptor to inhibit the iron absorption?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ferroportin
  • Hepcidin acts on: B. Ferroportin
  • DMT-1 is involved in iron uptake in enterocytes.
  • Hephaestin is responsible for converting ferrous to ferric iron for transport.
  • Transferrin is a blood transport protein for ferric iron.


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no: 477

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones do not act on pancreas?
questions.solutionHtml:
Gastrin
  • Gastrin does not act on the pancreas.
  • Gastrin stimulates gastric acid secretion and gastric mucosal growth.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no 792, 820. Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology - 25th Edition Page 452, 456-459.

questions.stem: Golgi tendon organ senses which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tension
  • The Golgi tendon organ (GTO) senses B. Tension.
  • When the muscle contracts and generates tension, the Golgi tendon organ is activated. It sends signals to the central nervous system (CNS) about the amount of force or tension being exerted by the muscle.
  • The Golgi tendon organ is a sensory receptor located at the junction of a muscle and its tendon (the point where the muscle fibers insert into the tendon). Its primary function is to monitor the tension or force generated by the muscle during contraction.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page nos 228 and 229.

questions.stem: Hormone exclusively secreted by the adrenal gland of females ?
questions.solutionHtml:
DHEA-S
  • The hormone DHEA-S (Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate) is exclusively secreted by the adrenal gland of females.
  • DHEA-S is a steroid hormone produced by the adrenal glands, which are located on top of the kidneys. Both males and females produce DHEA-S, but it is considered a predominantly female hormone because its production is much higher in females compared to males.


Shaw's Textbook of Gynecology 16th Edition Page no 551.
